html:
The leader of Kenya's independence movement and its first president, from 1964 to his death in 1978. He was a Kikuyu, the largest people of the central highlands, where white settlers had taken much of the land.

He spent most of 1931 to 1946 in Britain, campaigning on Kikuyu land rights. He studied anthropology in London and wrote Facing Mount Kenya (1938), a study of Kikuyu life. In 1945 he helped organise the Pan-African Congress in Manchester with Kwame Nkrumah.

Back in Kenya, he led the Kenya African Union. When the Mau Mau uprising broke out, the British arrested him in 1952 and jailed him after a trial now widely seen as unfair. He was freed in 1961, became prime minister in 1963 and president a year later.

In power he was moderate toward the West and the settlers, built a one-party state under KANU, and let land and wealth flow to a Kikuyu elite. His son Uhuru Kenyatta was president from 2013 to 2022.
